We've been friends for 10 years, and I've always known him as Tim. But apparently, he has an Icelandic name, Thor, and he's now insisting that people call him that. If they don't, he's cutting ties with them. I'm not sure how to handle this because I've been calling him Tim for so long, and it's just not easy to switch to Thor overnight. Plus, he has a short fuse, so I'm worried that if I slip up and call him Tim by accident, he'll get upset. First, I need to understand why he wants to be called Thor now. Is it because of his Icelandic heritage? Maybe he feels a stronger connection to his Icelandic name now. Or perhaps he's going through some identity changes and wants to be recognized by his Icelandic name. It's also possible that he feels that his Canadian name, Tim, doesn't fully represent who he is. I also need to consider how this affects our friendship. He's demanding that people call him Thor, and if they don't, he's ending the friendship. That seems pretty extreme. I value our friendship, but I'm not sure if I can just switch to calling him Thor without any issues. It's going to take time to get used to it, and I might make mistakes along the way. I wonder if there's a way to transition smoothly from Tim to Thor. Maybe I can start by using both names interchangeably and gradually shift to using Thor more often. But I'm not sure if that would work, especially since he has a short fuse and might not appreciate any mix-up. Another thing to think about is how this reflects on his character. Is he being reasonable in expecting everyone to switch to his Icelandic name? Or is he being too demanding? I mean, names are personal, and it's important to respect how someone wants to be addressed. But at the same time, it's been 10 years of calling him Tim, and that's a significant part of our shared history. I also need to consider how this affects me emotionally. I'm not sure if I'm ready to let that go. Maybe I should talk to him about this before the get-together. Maybe he's okay with being called Tim in certain contexts or by certain people, while being called Thor in others. Or perhaps he's open to a nickname that combines both names. It's worth asking him if there's a compromise that works for both of us. Another angle to consider is cultural sensitivity.
